newsitem.title: USA: Bulgarian debt prices rebound in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian debt prices rebound in late trade.

text.p: Bulgarian debt prices reversed losses suffered in early London trade following news the country's ruling Socialists agreed to discuss early elections with the opposition, emerging market debt sources said.
"The prices are up on news that Bulgaria's socialists agreed to discuss an early election," said one trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
At 1610 EST/2110 GMT, Bulgaria's IABs were 3/8 higher at 49-5/8 bid after falling as much as one percentage point earlier today in London.
The country's FLRB's were 3/4 higher at 36-7/8 bid and its discount bonds were one percentage point stronger at 55-1/2 bid.

A statement read to reporters after a meeting of the party's leadership in Sofia said: "We are ready to talk about early parliamentary elections in the context of the implementation of the anti-crisis program."

Elsewhere, Brazilian paper pared losses on news the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMBD) agreed to vote in congress on a constitutional amendment allowing for re-election of the president and other high officials.
Brazilian "C" bonds were 1/8 lower at 74-3/8 after falling as much as 1/2 in London earlier today.
"It is good news that the PMBD said it will go forward with the vote as scheduled. If you ask me, I think the president has enough votes to get it passed," said another emerging markets trader.
In the broader market, traders said prices were narrowly mixed in extremely quiet trade.
Argentine pars were 1/4 firmer at 62-1/2 bid, Mexican UMS-26 were 1/2 weaker at 105-5/8 bid and Venezeulan DCBs were 1/2 better at 89-3/4 bid.
In other news, Venezuela's national telephone company CANTV said it applied to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to issue up to $150 million in five-year yankee bonds.
The bonds, which will be used to pay off some fo the company's $127.8 million restructured debt, will be lead managed by Chase Securities Inc and Goldman Sachs & Co.
